correctness.rationale: The open-state conjugacy is exact: for g(z)=Φ(z)-1/2, the update in the normal coordinate is z-a g(z). Strict decrease of q(u)=g(u)/u=∫₀¹φ(su)ds gives pointwise strict decrease in amplitude off zero for a<=2/φ(0); continuity excludes a positive limiting amplitude. At criticality the cubic term is +z³/3 after the linear term -z. Squaring yields v_next=v-(2/3)v²+O(v³), whose reciprocal increments tend to 2/3 as long as v never vanishes. This gives the two critical constants, with precisely the stated finite-hit exception. Adding the two displacement equations forces opposite points, and a q(u)=2 gives uniqueness iff a>a_c. The return multiplier is (1-aφ(u))². Along the branch aφ(u)=2/[∫₀¹exp(u²(1-s²)/2)ds] decreases strictly from 2 to 0; this gives stability, monotonicity on either side of the zero, and unique superstability. The expansion of q gives u²~6(a-a_c)/a_c. At large gain the exact identity a/4-u=(a/2)(1-Φ(u)) first gives u/a→1/4, then Mills' ratio gives a/4-u=O(φ(u)), hence φ(u)/φ(a/4)→1; substituting back yields all three stated constants. An independent bracketed solve using the series for the integral of exp(-t²) gave u_s≈1.399985276878204 and a_s≈6.678663688751936. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed. The supercritical assertion is global uniqueness of the pair, but local attraction; no broader basin conclusion is needed.

value.rationale: An exact quantitative response law for the natural normal-quantile counterpart of the established logit model: the oscillation remains locally stable at every supercritical gain yet becomes almost neutral on a Gaussian scale, with an explicit unique gain of fastest linear relaxation and a sharp law at the flip. These distinctions are relevant when comparing feedback strengths and distributions, beyond a generic flip assertion. The value is for the deterministic map and its stated stability notions, not applied performance or a global supercritical classification.
